<a name='M-CudaCSharp-Arrays-DenseTensor`1-EigensystemHerm-CudaCSharp-Arrays-DenseTensor{`0},CudaCSharp-Arrays-DenseTensor{`0},CudaCSharp-Arrays-DenseTensor{`0},CudaCSharp-Solver-EigType-'></a>
### EigensystemHerm(overwriteValues,overwriteVectors,B,type) `method`

##### Summary

Calculate the eigenvalues (and eigenvectors) of this Hermitian matrix for the special eigen-problem -- $A V = V \Lambda$, or matrices pair A, `B` for the general one -- $A V = \Lambda B V$ or $A B V = \Lambda V$ or $B A V = \Lambda V$ . Here, matrix A is this matrix.

##### Returns

The eigenvalues and the eigenvectors.

##### Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| overwriteValues | [CudaCSharp.Arrays.DenseTensor{\`0}](#T-CudaCSharp-Arrays-DenseTensor{`0} 'CudaCSharp.Arrays.DenseTensor{`0}') | the [DenseTensor\`1](#T-CudaCSharp-Arrays-DenseTensor`1 'CudaCSharp.Arrays.DenseTensor`1') to store eigenvalues, default null means that this method will create a new one and return |
| overwriteVectors | [CudaCSharp.Arrays.DenseTensor{\`0}](#T-CudaCSharp-Arrays-DenseTensor{`0} 'CudaCSharp.Arrays.DenseTensor{`0}') |  |
| B | [CudaCSharp.Arrays.DenseTensor{\`0}](#T-CudaCSharp-Arrays-DenseTensor{`0} 'CudaCSharp.Arrays.DenseTensor{`0}') | the input [DenseTensor\`1](#T-CudaCSharp-Arrays-DenseTensor`1 'CudaCSharp.Arrays.DenseTensor`1') to calculate general eigen-problem; if ` is null`, the normal eigen is performed and `type` is not used; otherwise, the general one is performed |
| type | [CudaCSharp.Solver.EigType](#T-CudaCSharp-Solver-EigType 'CudaCSharp.Solver.EigType') | the [EigType](#T-CudaCSharp-Solver-EigType 'CudaCSharp.Solver.EigType') to indicate positions of this matrix and `B` |

##### Exceptions

| Name | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| [System.NotSupportedException](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.NotSupportedException 'System.NotSupportedException') | if `T` is not one of the supported type |
| [System.ArgumentException](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.ArgumentException 'System.ArgumentException') | if any of the arguments or this tensor is not of supported shape |

### Reduce(reduction,α,opA,A,β,opC,C) `method`

##### Summary

Partial reduction of tensor `A`: $D_{\Pi^C(i_0,i_1,...,i_n)} = \alpha \Phi(\Psi_A(A_{\Pi^A(i_0,i_1,...,i_n)})) + \beta \Psi_C(C_{\Pi^C(i_0,i_1,...,i_n)})$. The missing indices of `A` compared to `C` will be aggregated according to `reduction`.

##### Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| reduction | [CudaCSharp.BinaryOperation](#T-CudaCSharp-BinaryOperation 'CudaCSharp.BinaryOperation') | the reduce [BinaryOperation](#T-CudaCSharp-BinaryOperation 'CudaCSharp.BinaryOperation')`Φ` |
| α | [\`0](#T-`0 '`0') | scalar α |
| opA | [CudaCSharp.UnitaryOperation](#T-CudaCSharp-UnitaryOperation 'CudaCSharp.UnitaryOperation') | [UnitaryOperation](#T-CudaCSharp-UnitaryOperation 'CudaCSharp.UnitaryOperation')`ΨA` |
| A | [CudaCSharp.Arrays.DenseTensor{\`0}](#T-CudaCSharp-Arrays-DenseTensor{`0} 'CudaCSharp.Arrays.DenseTensor{`0}') | [DenseTensor\`1](#T-CudaCSharp-Arrays-DenseTensor`1 'CudaCSharp.Arrays.DenseTensor`1') A |
| β | [\`0](#T-`0 '`0') | scalar β, default 0 |
| opC | [CudaCSharp.UnitaryOperation](#T-CudaCSharp-UnitaryOperation 'CudaCSharp.UnitaryOperation') | [UnitaryOperation](#T-CudaCSharp-UnitaryOperation 'CudaCSharp.UnitaryOperation')`ΨC`, default identity |
| C | [CudaCSharp.Arrays.DenseTensor{\`0}](#T-CudaCSharp-Arrays-DenseTensor{`0} 'CudaCSharp.Arrays.DenseTensor{`0}') | [DenseTensor\`1](#T-CudaCSharp-Arrays-DenseTensor`1 'CudaCSharp.Arrays.DenseTensor`1') C, default null |

##### Remarks

If `C` is null, or `β` is zero, this tensor itself will be used instead of `C`.

<a name='T-CudaCSharp-DiagType'></a>
## DiagType `type`

##### Namespace

CudaCSharp

##### Summary

The DiagType type indicates whether the main diagonal of the dense matrix is unity and consequently should not be touched or modified by the function. 
Its values correspond to Fortran characters ‘N’ or ‘n’ (non-unit) and ‘U’ or ‘u’ (unit) that are often used as parameters to legacy BLAS implementations.

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-DiagType-NonUnit'></a>
### NonUnit `constants`

##### Summary

the matrix diagonal has non-unit elements

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-DiagType-Unit'></a>
### Unit `constants`

##### Summary

the matrix diagonal has unit elements

<a name='T-CudaCSharp-SparseBlas-Cuda-Direction'></a>
## Direction `type`

##### Namespace

CudaCSharp.SparseBlas.Cuda

##### Summary

This type indicates whether the elements of a dense matrix should be parsed by rows or by columns (assuming column-major storage in memory of the dense matrix) in function `cusparse[S|D|C|Z]nnz`. Besides storage format of blocks in BSR format is also controlled by this type.

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-SparseBlas-Cuda-Direction-Column'></a>
### Column `constants`

##### Summary

the matrix should be parsed by columns

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-SparseBlas-Cuda-Direction-Row'></a>
### Row `constants`

##### Summary

the matrix should be parsed by rows

| incx | [System.Int32](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int32 'System.Int32') | stride between consecutive elements of `x` |

<a name='M-CudaCSharp-Blas-IBlas-Copy``1-System-Int32,CudaCSharp-Memory-Storage{``0},System-Int32,CudaCSharp-Memory-Storage{``0},System-Int32-'></a>
### Copy\`\`1(n,x,incx,y,incy) `method`

##### Summary

This function copies the vector `x` into the vector `y`. Hence, the performed operation is `y[j] = x[k] for i = 1,…,n; k = 1 + (i - 1)*incx and j = 1 + (i - 1)*incy`.

##### Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| n | [System.Int32](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int32 'System.Int32') | number of elements in the vector `x` and `y` |
| x | [CudaCSharp.Memory.Storage{\`\`0}](#T-CudaCSharp-Memory-Storage{``0} 'CudaCSharp.Memory.Storage{``0}') | vector with `n` elements |
| incx | [System.Int32](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int32 'System.Int32') | stride between consecutive elements of `x` |
| y | [CudaCSharp.Memory.Storage{\`\`0}](#T-CudaCSharp-Memory-Storage{``0} 'CudaCSharp.Memory.Storage{``0}') | vector with `n` elements |
| incy | [System.Int32](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int32 'System.Int32') | stride between consecutive elements of `y` |

<a name='M-CudaCSharp-Blas-IBlas-DiagonalMatrixMultiplyGeneral``1-CudaCSharp-SideMode,System-Int32,System-Int32,CudaCSharp-Memory-Storage{``0},System-Int32,CudaCSharp-Memory-Storage{``0},System-Int32,CudaCSharp-Memory-Storage{``0},System-Int32-'></a>
### DiagonalMatrixMultiplyGeneral\`\`1(mode,m,n,A,lda,x,incx,C,ldc) `method`

##### Summary

This function performs the matrix-matrix multiplication `C` = `A` diag(`x`) if `mode` == [Right](#F-CudaCSharp-SideMode-Right 'CudaCSharp.SideMode.Right') or `C` = diag(`x`) * `A` otherwise.

##### Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |

<a name='M-CudaCSharp-IDecomposable`3-EigensystemHerm-`1,`0,`0,CudaCSharp-Solver-EigType-'></a>
### EigensystemHerm(overwriteValues,overwriteVectors,B,type) `method`

##### Summary

Calculate the eigenvalues (and eigenvectors) of this Hermitian matrix for the special eigen-problem -- $A V = V \Lambda$, or matrices pair A, `B` for the general one -- $A V = \Lambda B V$ or $A B V = \Lambda V$ or $B A V = \Lambda V$ . Here, matrix A is this matrix.

##### Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| overwriteValues | [\`1](#T-`1 '`1') | the `TVec` to store eigenvalues, default null means that this method will create a new one and return |
| overwriteVectors | [\`0](#T-`0 '`0') | the `TMat` to store eigenvectors, default null means that this method will create a new one and return |
| B | [\`0](#T-`0 '`0') | the input `TMat` to calculate general eigen-problem; if ` is null`, the normal eigen is performed and `type` is not used; otherwise, the general one is performed |
| type | [CudaCSharp.Solver.EigType](#T-CudaCSharp-Solver-EigType 'CudaCSharp.Solver.EigType') | the [EigType](#T-CudaCSharp-Solver-EigType 'CudaCSharp.Solver.EigType') to indicate positions of this matrix and `B` |

| Name | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| [System.NotSupportedException](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.NotSupportedException 'System.NotSupportedException') | if `T` is not one of the supported type |

##### Summary

| overwrite | [\`0](#T-`0 '`0') | the `TMat` to overwrite by result, default null |

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| n | [System.Int32](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int32 'System.Int32') | number of rows and columns of `A` and `B` |

| ldvl | [System.Int32](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int32 'System.Int32') | the leading dimension of `leftVec` |

| lda | [System.Int32](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int32 'System.Int32') | leading dimension of `A` |

### LinearSolve\`\`1(n,nrhs,A,lda,B,ldb) `method`

##### Summary

Solve a series of linear systems: $A X = B$, where each column pair of X and `B` is a linear system. 
Both `A` and `B` are in-place where `A` is replaced by its LU decomposition and `B` the solution X.

##### Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| n | [System.Int32](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int32 'System.Int32') | number of rows and columns of matrix `A` |
| nrhs | [System.Int32](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int32 'System.Int32') | number of right-hand sides. |
| A | [CudaCSharp.Memory.Storage{\`\`0}](#T-CudaCSharp-Memory-Storage{``0} 'CudaCSharp.Memory.Storage{``0}') | the coefficient matrix |
| lda | [System.Int32](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int32 'System.Int32') | leading dimension of `A` |
| B | [CudaCSharp.Memory.Storage{\`\`0}](#T-CudaCSharp-Memory-Storage{``0} 'CudaCSharp.Memory.Storage{``0}') | each column of this matrix is the vector at right; overwritten by solution X in the end |
| ldb | [System.Int32](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int32 'System.Int32') | leading dimension of `B` |

### SingularValues\`\`2(jobu,jobvt,m,n,A,lda,S,U,ldu,Vct,ldVct) `method`

##### Summary

This function computes the singular value decomposition (SVD) of a matrix `A` and corresponding the left and/or right singular vectors: $A = U S V^*$.

##### Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| jobu | [CudaCSharp.Solver.SVDStore](#T-CudaCSharp-Solver-SVDStore 'CudaCSharp.Solver.SVDStore') | specifies options for computing all or part of the matrix `U` |
| jobvt | [CudaCSharp.Solver.SVDStore](#T-CudaCSharp-Solver-SVDStore 'CudaCSharp.Solver.SVDStore') | specifies options for computing all or part of the matrix `Vct`, same as `jobu` |
| m | [System.Int32](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int32 'System.Int32') | number of rows of matrix |
| n | [System.Int32](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int32 'System.Int32') | number of columns of matrix |
| A | [CudaCSharp.Memory.Storage{\`\`0}](#T-CudaCSharp-Memory-Storage{``0} 'CudaCSharp.Memory.Storage{``0}') | matrix with size `m`×`n` and leading dimension `lda` |
| lda | [System.Int32](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int32 'System.Int32') | leading dimension of `A` |
| S | [CudaCSharp.Memory.Storage{\`\`1}](#T-CudaCSharp-Memory-Storage{``1} 'CudaCSharp.Memory.Storage{``1}') | output singular values of size `min(, )`, must be pre-allocated and of corresponding real type |
| U | [CudaCSharp.Memory.Storage{\`\`0}](#T-CudaCSharp-Memory-Storage{``0} 'CudaCSharp.Memory.Storage{``0}') | left unitary matrix with size `ldu`×`m`, must be pre-allocated |
| ldu | [System.Int32](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int32 'System.Int32') | leading dimension of `U` |
| Vct | [CudaCSharp.Memory.Storage{\`\`0}](#T-CudaCSharp-Memory-Storage{``0} 'CudaCSharp.Memory.Storage{``0}') | right unitary ($V^*$) matrix with size `ldVct`×`n`, must be pre-allocated |

<a name='M-CudaCSharp-Tensor-ITensor-Contract``1-``0,CudaCSharp-Memory-Storage{``0},System-Int32[],System-Int64[],CudaCSharp-Memory-Storage{``0},System-Int32[],System-Int64[],``0,CudaCSharp-Memory-Storage{``0},System-Int32[],System-Int64[],CudaCSharp-Memory-Storage{``0}-'></a>
### Contract\`\`1(α,A,modeA,sizeA,β,B,modeB,sizeB,C,modeC,sizeC,D) `method`

##### Summary

Contract two tensors `A` and `B`: $D_{i_0,i_1,...,i_n} = \alpha \sum_{j_a = k_b}{A_{j_0,j_1,...,j_p} \cdot B_{k_0,k_1,...,k_q}} + \beta C_{i_0,i_1,...,i_n}$;

##### Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| α | [\`\`0](#T-``0 '``0') | scalar α |
| A | [CudaCSharp.Memory.Storage{\`\`0}](#T-CudaCSharp-Memory-Storage{``0} 'CudaCSharp.Memory.Storage{``0}') | tensor A |
| modeA | [System.Int32[]](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int32[] 'System.Int32[]') | mode of `A` |
| sizeA | [System.Int64[]](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int64[] 'System.Int64[]') | size/extent of `A` |
| β | [CudaCSharp.Memory.Storage{\`\`0}](#T-CudaCSharp-Memory-Storage{``0} 'CudaCSharp.Memory.Storage{``0}') | scalar β |
| B | [System.Int32[]](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int32[] 'System.Int32[]') | tensor B |
| modeB | [System.Int64[]](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int64[] 'System.Int64[]') | mode of `B` |
| sizeB | [\`\`0](#T-``0 '``0') | size/extent of `B` |
| C | [CudaCSharp.Memory.Storage{\`\`0}](#T-CudaCSharp-Memory-Storage{``0} 'CudaCSharp.Memory.Storage{``0}') | tensor C |
| modeC | [System.Int32[]](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int32[] 'System.Int32[]') | mode of tensor `D` and `C` |
| sizeC | [System.Int64[]](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int64[] 'System.Int64[]') | size/extent of `C` |
| D | [CudaCSharp.Memory.Storage{\`\`0}](#T-CudaCSharp-Memory-Storage{``0} 'CudaCSharp.Memory.Storage{``0}') | output tensor D |

##### Remarks

For example, if you want to contract a 4-tensor `ijkl` and a 3-tensor `kmi` to a 3-tensor `mjl`, then `modeA` can be `{0,1,2,3}`, `modeB` be `{2,4,0}` and `modeC` be `{4,1,3}`.

<a name='M-CudaCSharp-Tensor-ITensor-Permute``1-CudaCSharp-Memory-Storage{``0},System-Int64[],``0,CudaCSharp-UnitaryOperation,System-Int32[],CudaCSharp-Memory-Storage{``0},System-Int64[],System-Int32[]-'></a>
### Permute\`\`1(modeA,α,op,A,sizeA,B,sizeB,modeB) `method`

##### Summary

Permute (general transpose) and scale this tensor to form a new tensor: $B_{i_0,i_1,...,i_n} = \alpha \Psi(A_{\Pi(i_0,i_1,...,i_n)})$.

##### Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| modeA | [CudaCSharp.Memory.Storage{\`\`0}](#T-CudaCSharp-Memory-Storage{``0} 'CudaCSharp.Memory.Storage{``0}') | the order of `A` |
| α | [System.Int64[]](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int64[] 'System.Int64[]') | the scalar to multiply |
| op | [\`\`0](#T-``0 '``0') | the [UnitaryOperation](#T-CudaCSharp-UnitaryOperation 'CudaCSharp.UnitaryOperation')`Ψ` to apply on each element before scaling |
| A | [CudaCSharp.UnitaryOperation](#T-CudaCSharp-UnitaryOperation 'CudaCSharp.UnitaryOperation') | the source tensor |
| sizeA | [System.Int32[]](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int32[] 'System.Int32[]') | size/extent of `A` |
| B | [CudaCSharp.Memory.Storage{\`\`0}](#T-CudaCSharp-Memory-Storage{``0} 'CudaCSharp.Memory.Storage{``0}') | the output tensor |
| sizeB | [System.Int64[]](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int64[] 'System.Int64[]') | size/extent of `B` |
| modeB | [System.Int32[]](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int32[] 'System.Int32[]') | the order of `B` |

<a name='M-CudaCSharp-Tensor-ITensor-Reduce``1-CudaCSharp-BinaryOperation,``0,CudaCSharp-UnitaryOperation,CudaCSharp-Memory-Storage{``0},System-Int32[],System-Int64[],``0,CudaCSharp-UnitaryOperation,CudaCSharp-Memory-Storage{``0},System-Int32[],System-Int64[],CudaCSharp-Memory-Storage{``0}-'></a>
### Reduce\`\`1(reduction,α,opA,A,modeA,sizeA,β,opC,C,modeC,sizeC,D) `method`

##### Summary

Partial reduction of tensor `A`: $D_{\Pi^C(i_0,i_1,...,i_n)} = \alpha \Phi(\Psi_A(A_{\Pi^A(i_0,i_1,...,i_n)})) + \beta \Psi_C(C_{\Pi^C(i_0,i_1,...,i_n)})$. The missing indices of `modeA` compared to `modeC` will be aggregated according to `reduction`.

##### Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| reduction | [CudaCSharp.BinaryOperation](#T-CudaCSharp-BinaryOperation 'CudaCSharp.BinaryOperation') | the reduce [BinaryOperation](#T-CudaCSharp-BinaryOperation 'CudaCSharp.BinaryOperation')`Φ` |
| α | [\`\`0](#T-``0 '``0') | scalar α |
| opA | [CudaCSharp.UnitaryOperation](#T-CudaCSharp-UnitaryOperation 'CudaCSharp.UnitaryOperation') | [UnitaryOperation](#T-CudaCSharp-UnitaryOperation 'CudaCSharp.UnitaryOperation')`ΨA` |
| A | [CudaCSharp.Memory.Storage{\`\`0}](#T-CudaCSharp-Memory-Storage{``0} 'CudaCSharp.Memory.Storage{``0}') | tensor A |
| modeA | [System.Int32[]](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int32[] 'System.Int32[]') | mode of `A` |
| sizeA | [System.Int64[]](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int64[] 'System.Int64[]') | size/extent of `A` |
| β | [\`\`0](#T-``0 '``0') | scalar β, default 0 |
| opC | [CudaCSharp.UnitaryOperation](#T-CudaCSharp-UnitaryOperation 'CudaCSharp.UnitaryOperation') | [UnitaryOperation](#T-CudaCSharp-UnitaryOperation 'CudaCSharp.UnitaryOperation')`ΨC` |
| C | [CudaCSharp.Memory.Storage{\`\`0}](#T-CudaCSharp-Memory-Storage{``0} 'CudaCSharp.Memory.Storage{``0}') | tensor C |
| modeC | [System.Int32[]](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int32[] 'System.Int32[]') | mode of tensor `D` and `C` |
| sizeC | [System.Int64[]](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int64[] 'System.Int64[]') | size/extent of `C` |
| D | [CudaCSharp.Memory.Storage{\`\`0}](#T-CudaCSharp-Memory-Storage{``0} 'CudaCSharp.Memory.Storage{``0}') | output tensor D |

##### Remarks

For example, if you want to reduce a 4-tensor `ijkl` to a 2-tensor `il`, then `modeA` can be `{0,1,2,3}` and `modeC` be `{0,3}`.

<a name='T-CudaCSharp-General-KrylovSolver'></a>
## KrylovSolver `type`

##### Namespace

CudaCSharp.General

##### Summary

The solver class for Krylov subspace algorithms for eigen problem and linear system problem

<a name='M-CudaCSharp-General-KrylovSolver-KrylovSchur``2-System-Func{``0,``0},``0,System-Int64,System-Int32,CudaCSharp-General-KrylovSolver-WhichEigenvalues,System-Int32,System-Int32,System-Double,System-Boolean,System-Boolean,CudaCSharp-General-RestartStrategy,CudaCSharp-General-IRestartStrategy-'></a>
### KrylovSchur\`\`2(MatMulVecFunc,initial,size,nEig,which,tolerance,maxRestarts,iterPerRestart,robustOrthogonalize,useGap,strategy,restartStrategy) `method`

##### Summary

The Krylov-Schur algorithm for non-Hermitian matrix's partial (especially the extreme eigenvalues) eigen-problem.

##### Returns

An array of [DoubleComplex](#T-CudaCSharp-DoubleComplex 'CudaCSharp.DoubleComplex') as the eigenvalues and an array of `TVec` as corresponding eigenvectors (and a possible imaginary part of eigenvectors if `T` is not a complex type) and the convergence at last.

##### Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| MatMulVecFunc | [System.Func{\`\`0,\`\`0}](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Func 'System.Func{``0,``0}') | a function that receives a dense vector input and give the result of the multiplication of the non-Hermitian matrix and the input vector |
| initial | [\`\`0](#T-``0 '``0') | the initial vector |
| size | [System.Int64](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int64 'System.Int64') | matrix size |
| nEig | [System.Int32](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int32 'System.Int32') | only the top `nEig` eigenvalues are the target, we DO NOT recommend a large value since the Krylov-Schur algorithm is not designed for it |
| which | [CudaCSharp.General.KrylovSolver.WhichEigenvalues](#T-CudaCSharp-General-KrylovSolver-WhichEigenvalues 'CudaCSharp.General.KrylovSolver.WhichEigenvalues') | a [WhichEigenvalues](#T-CudaCSharp-General-KrylovSolver-WhichEigenvalues 'CudaCSharp.General.KrylovSolver.WhichEigenvalues') to indicate which eigen-pairs are desired |
| tolerance | [System.Int32](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int32 'System.Int32') | the threshold of convergence, default 0 means `machine precision * 5` |
| maxRestarts | [System.Int32](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int32 'System.Int32') | max number of restarts |
| iterPerRestart | [System.Double](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Double 'System.Double') | iteration number per restart, default 0 means auto calculation |
| robustOrthogonalize | [System.Boolean](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Boolean 'System.Boolean') | perform robust orthogonalization or not, default `true` |
| useGap | [System.Boolean](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Boolean 'System.Boolean') | use the estimated gap in the convergence criteria or use the matrix norm, default true |
| strategy | [CudaCSharp.General.RestartStrategy](#T-CudaCSharp-General-RestartStrategy 'CudaCSharp.General.RestartStrategy') | the restart strategy to use, if it is [UserDefine](#F-CudaCSharp-General-RestartStrategy-UserDefine 'CudaCSharp.General.RestartStrategy.UserDefine'), the `restartStrategy` must be indicated |
| restartStrategy | [CudaCSharp.General.IRestartStrategy](#T-CudaCSharp-General-IRestartStrategy 'CudaCSharp.General.IRestartStrategy') | used for selecting the preservation Ritz pairs only when `strategy` is [UserDefine](#F-CudaCSharp-General-RestartStrategy-UserDefine 'CudaCSharp.General.RestartStrategy.UserDefine') |

##### Generic Types

| Name | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| T | the data type, see [AbstractArray\`1](#T-CudaCSharp-AbstractArray`1 'CudaCSharp.AbstractArray`1') for more information |
| TVec | the general dense vector type that inherits [AbstractArray\`1](#T-CudaCSharp-AbstractArray`1 'CudaCSharp.AbstractArray`1'), [IKrylovVector\`2](#T-CudaCSharp-General-IKrylovVector`2 'CudaCSharp.General.IKrylovVector`2') and must be a concrete class type |

##### Exceptions

| Name | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| [System.ArgumentException](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.ArgumentException 'System.ArgumentException') | if any of the arguments is wrong |
| [System.InvalidOperationException](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.InvalidOperationException 'System.InvalidOperationException') | if the `MatMulVecFunc` throws inner exceptions |
| [System.InsufficientMemoryException](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.InsufficientMemoryException 'System.InsufficientMemoryException') | if the `nEig` is too large to be calculated within free memory |

##### Remarks

Currently, if some eigen-pairs are not converged after maximum number of iterations, they will not be returned.

<a name='M-CudaCSharp-General-KrylovSolver-LinearSolve``2-System-Func{``0,``0},``0,System-Int64,``0,System-Int32,System-Int32,System-Double,System-Boolean-'></a>
### LinearSolve\`\`2(MatMulVecFunc,b,initGuess,size,tolerance,maxRestarts,iterPerRestart,robustOrthogonalize) `method`

##### Summary

The Krylov subspace algorithm for non-Hermitian matrix's linear system problem, a.k.a. GMRES (solve `x` for `MatMulVecFunc`(`x`) = `b`).

##### Returns

A `TVec` as corresponding solve and a [Double](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Double 'System.Double') as the relative error.

##### Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| MatMulVecFunc | [System.Func{\`\`0,\`\`0}](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Func 'System.Func{``0,``0}') | a function that receives a dense vector input and give the result of the multiplication of the non-Hermitian matrix and the input vector |
| b | [\`\`0](#T-``0 '``0') | the vector b |
| initGuess | [System.Int64](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int64 'System.Int64') | the initial guess vector |
| size | [\`\`0](#T-``0 '``0') | matrix size |
| tolerance | [System.Int32](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int32 'System.Int32') | the threshold of convergence, default 0 means `machine precision * 5` |
| maxRestarts | [System.Int32](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int32 'System.Int32') | max number of restarts |
| iterPerRestart | [System.Double](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Double 'System.Double') | iteration number per restart, default 0 means auto calculation |
| robustOrthogonalize | [System.Boolean](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Boolean 'System.Boolean') | perform robust orthogonalization or not, default `true` |

##### Generic Types

| Name | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| T | the data type, see [AbstractArray\`1](#T-CudaCSharp-AbstractArray`1 'CudaCSharp.AbstractArray`1') for more information |
| TVec | the general dense vector type that inherits [AbstractArray\`1](#T-CudaCSharp-AbstractArray`1 'CudaCSharp.AbstractArray`1'), [IKrylovVector\`2](#T-CudaCSharp-General-IKrylovVector`2 'CudaCSharp.General.IKrylovVector`2') and must be a concrete class type |

##### Exceptions

| Name | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| [System.ArgumentException](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.ArgumentException 'System.ArgumentException') | if any of the arguments is wrong |
| [System.InvalidOperationException](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.InvalidOperationException 'System.InvalidOperationException') | if the `MatMulVecFunc` throws inner exceptions |

##### Remarks

Currently, if some eigen-pairs are not converged after maximum number of iterations, they will not be returned.

<a name='T-CudaCSharp-General-LanczosSolver'></a>
## LanczosSolver `type`

##### Namespace

CudaCSharp.General

##### Summary

The Lanczos solvers API.

<a name='M-CudaCSharp-General-LanczosSolver-Lanczos``2-System-Func{``0,``0},``0,System-Int64,System-Int32,System-Int32,System-Double,CudaCSharp-General-ReorthogonalizeMethod,System-Boolean,CudaCSharp-General-RestartStrategy,CudaCSharp-General-IRestartStrategy-'></a>
### Lanczos\`\`2(MatMulVecFunc,initial,size,smallestK,tolerance,maxIter,reorthogonalize,useGap,strategy,selector) `method`

##### Summary

Lanczos algorithm for Hermitian matrix's partial (especially the lowest eigenvalues) eigen-problem.

##### Returns

An array of [Double](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Double 'System.Double') as the eigenvalues and an array of `TVec` as corresponding eigenvectors and the convergence.

##### Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| MatMulVecFunc | [System.Func{\`\`0,\`\`0}](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Func 'System.Func{``0,``0}') | a function that receives a dense vector input and give the result of the multiplication of the Hermitian matrix and the input vector |
| initial | [\`\`0](#T-``0 '``0') | the initial vector |
| size | [System.Int64](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int64 'System.Int64') | matrix size |
| smallestK | [System.Int32](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int32 'System.Int32') | only the smallest k eigenvalues are the target, we DO NOT recommend a larger k since Lanczos is not designed for it |
| tolerance | [System.Int32](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int32 'System.Int32') | the tolerance of the Lanczos iterative solver, default 0 means `machine precision * 5` |
| maxIter | [System.Double](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Double 'System.Double') | max iteration number, if `maxIter` ≤ 0, it will be auto calculated and the thick restart strategy will be used to compute multiple eigen-pairs until they are all converged; otherwise, the computation stops at total number of iterations = `maxIter` while some of the eigen-pairs may not be calculated at all |
| reorthogonalize | [CudaCSharp.General.ReorthogonalizeMethod](#T-CudaCSharp-General-ReorthogonalizeMethod 'CudaCSharp.General.ReorthogonalizeMethod') | perform re-orthogonalization or not, default is `true`, (notice that Lanczos algorithm is extremely numerical unstable without it) |
| useGap | [System.Boolean](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Boolean 'System.Boolean') | use the estimated gap in the convergence criteria or use the matrix norm, default true |
| strategy | [CudaCSharp.General.RestartStrategy](#T-CudaCSharp-General-RestartStrategy 'CudaCSharp.General.RestartStrategy') | the restart strategy to use, if it is [UserDefine](#F-CudaCSharp-General-RestartStrategy-UserDefine 'CudaCSharp.General.RestartStrategy.UserDefine'), the `selector` must be indicated |
| selector | [CudaCSharp.General.IRestartStrategy](#T-CudaCSharp-General-IRestartStrategy 'CudaCSharp.General.IRestartStrategy') | used for selecting the preservation Ritz pairs only when `strategy` is [UserDefine](#F-CudaCSharp-General-RestartStrategy-UserDefine 'CudaCSharp.General.RestartStrategy.UserDefine') |

##### Generic Types

| Name | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| T | the data type, see [AbstractArray\`1](#T-CudaCSharp-AbstractArray`1 'CudaCSharp.AbstractArray`1') for more information |
| TVec | the general dense vector type that inherits [AbstractArray\`1](#T-CudaCSharp-AbstractArray`1 'CudaCSharp.AbstractArray`1'), [IKrylovVector\`2](#T-CudaCSharp-General-IKrylovVector`2 'CudaCSharp.General.IKrylovVector`2') and must be a concrete class type |

##### Exceptions

| Name | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| [System.ArgumentException](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.ArgumentException 'System.ArgumentException') | if any of the arguments is wrong |
| [System.InvalidOperationException](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.InvalidOperationException 'System.InvalidOperationException') | if the `MatMulVecFunc` throws inner exceptions |
| [System.InsufficientMemoryException](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.InsufficientMemoryException 'System.InsufficientMemoryException') | if the `smallestK` is too large to be calculated within free memory |

##### Remarks

Currently, if some eigen-pairs are not converged after maximum number of iterations, they will not be returned.

### From_αA_Add_βB(α,A,opA,β,B,opB) `method`

##### Summary

| A | [CudaCSharp.Arrays.MatrixBase{\`0}](#T-CudaCSharp-Arrays-MatrixBase{`0} 'CudaCSharp.Arrays.MatrixBase{`0}') | the [MatrixBase\`1](#T-CudaCSharp-Arrays-MatrixBase`1 'CudaCSharp.Arrays.MatrixBase`1') A, can be null |
| opA | [\`0](#T-`0 '`0') | operation to matrix `A` |

| B | [CudaCSharp.MatrixOperation](#T-CudaCSharp-MatrixOperation 'CudaCSharp.MatrixOperation') | the input [MatrixBase\`1](#T-CudaCSharp-Arrays-MatrixBase`1 'CudaCSharp.Arrays.MatrixBase`1') B, can be null |
| opB | [CudaCSharp.MatrixOperation](#T-CudaCSharp-MatrixOperation 'CudaCSharp.MatrixOperation') | operation to matrix `B` |

| [System.ArgumentException](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.ArgumentException 'System.ArgumentException') | if the arrays do not match in size |

<a name='M-CudaCSharp-Arrays-MatrixBase`1-From_αA_Add_βB_Opposite-CudaCSharp-Arrays-MatrixBase{`0},CudaCSharp-Arrays-MatrixBase{`0},`0,`0,CudaCSharp-MatrixOperation,CudaCSharp-MatrixOperation-'></a>
### From_αA_Add_βB_Opposite(α,C,opA,β,B,opB) `method`

##### Summary

Compute $C = \alpha opA(A_{\text{this}}) + \beta B^{\text{opB}}$ (this matrix is `A`).

##### Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| α | [CudaCSharp.Arrays.MatrixBase{\`0}](#T-CudaCSharp-Arrays-MatrixBase{`0} 'CudaCSharp.Arrays.MatrixBase{`0}') | scalar of type `T` with default 0. If ` == 0`, `A` can be an invalid input |
| C | [CudaCSharp.Arrays.MatrixBase{\`0}](#T-CudaCSharp-Arrays-MatrixBase{`0} 'CudaCSharp.Arrays.MatrixBase{`0}') | the output [MatrixBase\`1](#T-CudaCSharp-Arrays-MatrixBase`1 'CudaCSharp.Arrays.MatrixBase`1') C, cannot be null |
| opA | [\`0](#T-`0 '`0') | operation to matrix `A` |
| β | [\`0](#T-`0 '`0') | scalar of type `T` with default 0. If ` == 0`, `B` can be an invalid input |
| B | [CudaCSharp.MatrixOperation](#T-CudaCSharp-MatrixOperation 'CudaCSharp.MatrixOperation') | the input [MatrixBase\`1](#T-CudaCSharp-Arrays-MatrixBase`1 'CudaCSharp.Arrays.MatrixBase`1') B, can be null |
| opB | [CudaCSharp.MatrixOperation](#T-CudaCSharp-MatrixOperation 'CudaCSharp.MatrixOperation') | operation to matrix `B` |

##### Exceptions

| Name | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| [System.ArgumentNullException](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.ArgumentNullException 'System.ArgumentNullException') | if all of the array are null |
| [System.ArgumentException](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.ArgumentException 'System.ArgumentException') | if the arrays do not match in size |
| [CudaCSharp.StatusException](#T-CudaCSharp-StatusException 'CudaCSharp.StatusException') | if the internal returns error status |

##### Remarks

If the returned matrix is same as `A` or `B`, no new matrix will be created and `C` will not be altered.
This is the opposite operation of [From_αA_Add_βB](#M-CudaCSharp-Arrays-MatrixBase`1-From_αA_Add_βB-CudaCSharp-Arrays-MatrixBase{`0},CudaCSharp-Arrays-MatrixBase{`0},`0,`0,CudaCSharp-MatrixOperation,CudaCSharp-MatrixOperation- 'CudaCSharp.Arrays.MatrixBase`1.From_αA_Add_βB(CudaCSharp.Arrays.MatrixBase{`0},CudaCSharp.Arrays.MatrixBase{`0},`0,`0,CudaCSharp.MatrixOperation,CudaCSharp.MatrixOperation)'), and is not implemented by built-in matrix classes while is used by them to support other possible matrix classes inherit from [MatrixBase\`1](#T-CudaCSharp-Arrays-MatrixBase`1 'CudaCSharp.Arrays.MatrixBase`1') in operation [From_αA_Add_βB](#M-CudaCSharp-Arrays-MatrixBase`1-From_αA_Add_βB-CudaCSharp-Arrays-MatrixBase{`0},CudaCSharp-Arrays-MatrixBase{`0},`0,`0,CudaCSharp-MatrixOperation,CudaCSharp-MatrixOperation- 'CudaCSharp.Arrays.MatrixBase`1.From_αA_Add_βB(CudaCSharp.Arrays.MatrixBase{`0},CudaCSharp.Arrays.MatrixBase{`0},`0,`0,CudaCSharp.MatrixOperation,CudaCSharp.MatrixOperation)'). Since `A` and `B` are symmetric parameters, this method is enough.

| ---- | ---- | ----------- |

| forceHerm | [System.Boolean](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Boolean 'System.Boolean') | if the result is made Hermitian or not |

##### Summary

From [KroneckerSum](#M-CudaCSharp-IMatrix`2-KroneckerSum-`0,System-Boolean,`0- 'CudaCSharp.IMatrix`2.KroneckerSum(`0,System.Boolean,`0)').

| forceHerm | [System.Boolean](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Boolean 'System.Boolean') | if the result is made Hermitian or not |

## NativeMethods `type`

##### Namespace

CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.Xt

##### Summary

The cublasXt API supports only the compute-intensive BLAS3 routines (e.g matrix-matrix operations) where the PCI transfers back and forth from the GPU can be amortized. 
It takes care of allocating the memory across the designated GPUs and dispatched the workload between them and finally retrieves the results back.

<a name='M-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-NativeMethods-cublasGetAtomicsMode-System-IntPtr,CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-AtomicsMode@-'></a>
### cublasGetAtomicsMode(handle,mode) `method`

##### Summary

Some routines like `cublas<t>symv` and `cublas<t>hemv` have an alternate implementation that use atomics to cumulate results. This implementation is generally significantly faster but can generate results that are not strictly identical from one run to the others. Mathematically, those different results are not significant but when debugging
those differences can be prejudicial.



This function queries the atomic mode of a specific cuBLAS context.

##### Returns

operation status enum [Status](#T-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-Status 'CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.Status')

##### Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| handle | [System.IntPtr](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.IntPtr 'System.IntPtr') | input CUDA BLAS handle |
| mode | [CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.AtomicsMode@](#T-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-AtomicsMode@ 'CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.AtomicsMode@') | returned [AtomicsMode](#T-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-AtomicsMode 'CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.AtomicsMode') |

##### Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| handle | [System.IntPtr](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.IntPtr 'System.IntPtr') | input CUDA BLAS handle |
| mode | [CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.PointerMode@](#T-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-PointerMode@ 'CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.PointerMode@') | returned [PointerMode](#T-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-PointerMode 'CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.PointerMode') |

<a name='M-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-NativeMethods-cublasSetAtomicsMode-System-IntPtr,CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-AtomicsMode-'></a>
### cublasSetAtomicsMode(handle,mode) `method`

##### Summary

Some routines like `cublas<t>symv` have an alternate implementation that use atomics to cumulate results. This implementation is generally significantly faster but can generate results that are not strictly identical from one run to the others. Mathematically, those different results are not significant but when debugging those differences can be prejudicial.



This function allows or disallows the usage of atomics in the CUDA BLAS library for all routines which have an alternate implementation.

##### Returns

operation status enum [Status](#T-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-Status 'CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.Status')

##### Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| handle | [System.IntPtr](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.IntPtr 'System.IntPtr') | input CUDA BLAS handle |
| mode | [CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.AtomicsMode](#T-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-AtomicsMode 'CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.AtomicsMode') | the [AtomicsMode](#T-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-AtomicsMode 'CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.AtomicsMode') to set |

<a name='M-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-NativeMethods-cublasSetPointerMode_v2-System-IntPtr,CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-PointerMode-'></a>
### cublasSetPointerMode_v2(handle,mode) `method`

##### Summary

This function sets the pointer mode used by the cuBLAS library.
The default is for the values to be passed by reference on the host.

##### Returns

operation status enum [Status](#T-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-Status 'CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.Status')

##### Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |

<a name='M-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-Xt-NativeMethods-cublasXtSetBlockDim-System-IntPtr,System-Int32-'></a>
### cublasXtSetBlockDim(handle,blockDim) `method`

##### Summary

This function allows the user to set the block dimension used for the tiling of the matrices  for the subsequent Math function calls.
Matrices are split in square tiles of blockDim×blockDim dimension.
This function can be called anytime and will take effect for the following Math function calls.
The block dimension should be chosen in a way to optimize the math operation and to make sure that the PCI transfers are well overlapped with the computation.

##### Returns

operation status enum [Status](#T-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-Status 'CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.Status')

##### Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| handle | [System.IntPtr](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.IntPtr 'System.IntPtr') | CUDA BLASXt context retrieved by [cublasXtCreate](#M-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-Xt-NativeMethods-cublasXtCreate-System-IntPtr@- 'CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.Xt.NativeMethods.cublasXtCreate(System.IntPtr@)') |
| blockDim | [System.Int32](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int32 'System.Int32') | block dimension to override |

<a name='M-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-Xt-NativeMethods-cublasXtSetCpuRatio-System-IntPtr,CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-XtOperationList,CudaCSharp-DataType,System-Single-'></a>
### cublasXtSetCpuRatio(handle,blasOp,type,ratio) `method`

##### Summary

This function allows the user to define the percentage of workload that should be done on a CPU in the context of an hybrid computation. This function can be used with the function [cublasXtSetCpuRoutine](#M-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-Xt-NativeMethods-cublasXtSetCpuRoutine-System-IntPtr,CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-XtOperationList,CudaCSharp-DataType,System-IntPtr- 'CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.Xt.NativeMethods.cublasXtSetCpuRoutine(System.IntPtr,CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.XtOperationList,CudaCSharp.DataType,System.IntPtr)') to define an hybrid computation between the CPU and the GPUs. By default, no CPU BLAS routine is used.
See https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cublas/index.html#cublasxt_setCpuRatio for more detail.

##### Returns

operation status enum [Status](#T-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-Status 'CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.Status')

##### Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| handle | [System.IntPtr](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.IntPtr 'System.IntPtr') | CUDA BLASXt context retrieved by [cublasXtCreate](#M-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-Xt-NativeMethods-cublasXtCreate-System-IntPtr@- 'CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.Xt.NativeMethods.cublasXtCreate(System.IntPtr@)') |
| blasOp | [CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.XtOperationList](#T-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-XtOperationList 'CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.XtOperationList') | one of the enum [XtOperationList](#T-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-XtOperationList 'CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.XtOperationList') to indicate the routine to specify |
| type | [CudaCSharp.DataType](#T-CudaCSharp-DataType 'CudaCSharp.DataType') | data type to of the routine to specify |
| ratio | [System.Single](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Single 'System.Single') | ratio of the CPU BLAS routine |

##### Remarks

Currently the hybrid feature is only supported for the [GEMM](#F-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-XtOperationList-GEMM 'CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.XtOperationList.GEMM') routines.

<a name='M-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-Xt-NativeMethods-cublasXtSetCpuRoutine-System-IntPtr,CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-XtOperationList,CudaCSharp-DataType,System-IntPtr-'></a>

##### Summary

Launches are done with the stream or the null stream if no stream has been set.



Results are 32-bit [Int32](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int32 'System.Int32') with every bit random.

<a name='T-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-PointerMode'></a>
## PointerMode `type`

##### Namespace

CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda

##### Summary

The PointerMode type indicates whether the scalar values are passed by reference on the host or device. 
It is important to point out that if several scalar values are present in the function call, all of them must conform to the same single pointer mode. 
The pointer mode can be set and retrieved using [cublasGetPointerMode_v2](#M-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-NativeMethods-cublasGetPointerMode_v2-System-IntPtr,CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-PointerMode@- 'CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.NativeMethods.cublasGetPointerMode_v2(System.IntPtr,CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.PointerMode@)') and [cublasSetPointerMode_v2](#M-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-NativeMethods-cublasSetPointerMode_v2-System-IntPtr,CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-PointerMode- 'CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.NativeMethods.cublasSetPointerMode_v2(System.IntPtr,CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.PointerMode)') routines, respectively.

<a name='T-CudaCSharp-Arrays-PureArray`1'></a>
## PureArray\`1 `type`

##### Namespace

CudaCSharp.Arrays

##### Summary

The abstract device array class for array whose [Pointer](#P-CudaCSharp-Arrays-PureArray`1-Pointer 'CudaCSharp.Arrays.PureArray`1.Pointer') only refers to the data array. There may be more pointer(s) standing for different indices in a sparse array, in which case the [Pointer](#P-CudaCSharp-Arrays-PureArray`1-Pointer 'CudaCSharp.Arrays.PureArray`1.Pointer') only refers to the value data array.

##### Generic Types

| Name | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| T | the supported data types are [Single](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Single 'System.Single'), [Double](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Double 'System.Double'), [FloatComplex](#T-CudaCSharp-FloatComplex 'CudaCSharp.FloatComplex'), [DoubleComplex](#T-CudaCSharp-DoubleComplex 'CudaCSharp.DoubleComplex'), other types of data may causes [NotSupportedException](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.NotSupportedException 'System.NotSupportedException') |

<a name='T-CudaCSharp-Linq-ReadOnlyListLinq'></a>
## ReadOnlyListLinq `type`

##### Namespace

CudaCSharp.Linq

##### Summary

A replacement of [Enumerable](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Linq.Enumerable 'System.Linq.Enumerable') since it produces too much garbage which leads to GC stress.
Methods of this class is based on [IReadOnlyList\`1](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList`1 'System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList`1') and is implemented by [Array](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Array 'System.Array') to minimize GC stress.

<a name='T-CudaCSharp-General-ReorthogonalizeMethod'></a>
## ReorthogonalizeMethod `type`

##### Namespace

CudaCSharp.General

##### Summary

The method used to re-orthogonalize with the previous basis in Lanczos

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-General-ReorthogonalizeMethod-Full'></a>
### Full `constants`

##### Summary

Perform full re-orthogonalization at each iteration, this may lead to extra performance loss, especially when the problem size is small. You can use this method when the [Selective](#F-CudaCSharp-General-ReorthogonalizeMethod-Selective 'CudaCSharp.General.ReorthogonalizeMethod.Selective') one does not perform well

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-General-ReorthogonalizeMethod-None'></a>
### None `constants`

##### Summary

Do not perform re-orthogonalization,

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-General-ReorthogonalizeMethod-RobustFull'></a>
### RobustFull `constants`

##### Summary

Perform robust full re-orthogonalization at each iteration, this may lead to extra performance loss, especially when the problem size is small. You can use this method when the [Selective](#F-CudaCSharp-General-ReorthogonalizeMethod-Selective 'CudaCSharp.General.ReorthogonalizeMethod.Selective') one does not perform well

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-General-ReorthogonalizeMethod-Selective'></a>
### Selective `constants`

##### Summary

Selective re-orthogonalize, let the internal heuristic to determine when and which basis to re-orthogonalize

<a name='T-CudaCSharp-General-RestartStrategy'></a>
## RestartStrategy `type`

##### Namespace

CudaCSharp.General

##### Summary

The strategy adopted by the thick restart Lanczos and Krylov-Shcur algorithm.

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-General-RestartStrategy-CurrentResidualBest'></a>
### CurrentResidualBest `constants`

##### Summary

Based on the residual of Ritz eigen-pairs, preserve the smallest $k$ ones: 
$$k=\underset{i}{\mathrm{argmax}}\left( \left| s_{n,i} \right| < \max\left\{ \sqrt{\left| s_{n,n_{\mathrm{eig}}} \right|\max_{j}\left| s_{n,j} \right|},2\left| s_{n,n_{\mathrm{eig}}} \right| \right\} \right)$$

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-General-RestartStrategy-IndexBased'></a>
### IndexBased `constants`

##### Summary

Based on the index of Ritz eigen-pairs, preserve the smallest $k$ ones: 
$$k=n_c+\min{\left\{n_{\mathrm{eig}},\left(p-n_c\right)\left(\frac{2}{5}+\frac{n_{\mathrm{eig}}}{10p}\right)\right\}}$$

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-General-RestartStrategy-KrylovSchur'></a>
### KrylovSchur `constants`

##### Summary

The heuristic used by Krylov-Schur algorithm to prevent stagnating

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-General-RestartStrategy-Naive'></a>
### Naive `constants`

##### Summary

The naïve strategy which only preserve the lowest Ritz eigen-pair and converged ones.

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-General-RestartStrategy-OneStepResidualImprove'></a>
### OneStepResidualImprove `constants`

##### Summary

Based on the improvement of residual of Ritz eigen-pairs of single iteration after the restart, preserve the smallest $k$ ones: 
$$k=\max{\left\{n_{\mathrm{eig}},\frac{3p+2n_c}{5}\right\}}$$

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-General-RestartStrategy-UserDefine'></a>
### UserDefine `constants`

##### Summary

User defined strategy

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-General-RestartStrategy-WholeIterResidualImprove'></a>
### WholeIterResidualImprove `constants`

##### Summary

Based on the improvement of residual of Ritz eigen-pairs of single iteration after the restart, preserve the smallest $k$ ones: 
$$k=\underset{k}{\max}{\left(p-k\right)\frac{\lambda_{k+1}-\lambda_1}{\lambda_m-\lambda_1}}$$

<a name='T-CudaCSharp-SideMode'></a>
## SideMode `type`

##### Namespace

CudaCSharp

##### Summary

The SideMode type indicates whether the dense matrix is on the left or right side in the matrix equation solved by a particular function. 
Its values correspond to Fortran characters ‘L’ or ‘l’ (left) and ‘R’ or ‘r’ (right) that are often used as parameters to legacy BLAS implementations.

<a name='T-CudaCSharp-Solver-Cuda-Sparse-NativeMethods-SpQRSolveFunc`1'></a>
## SpQRSolveFunc\`1 `type`

##### Namespace

CudaCSharp.Solver.Cuda.Sparse.NativeMethods

##### Summary

This function solves the linear system $A \vec{x} = \vec{b}$ where A is an `m`×`m` sparse matrix of [CSR](#F-CudaCSharp-SparseMatrixFormat-CSR 'CudaCSharp.SparseMatrixFormat.CSR'). `b` is the right-hand-side vector of size `m`, and `x` is the solution vector of size `m`. The supported matrix type is [General](#F-CudaCSharp-SparseBlas-Cuda-MatrixType-General 'CudaCSharp.SparseBlas.Cuda.MatrixType.General'). 
The linear system is solved by sparse QR factorization,  $A = Q R$. If A is singular under given tolerance, then some diagonal elements of R is zero, i.e. $|R(j, j)| < \text{tolerance}$ for some `j`. 
The output parameter singularity is the smallest index of such j. If A is non-singular, singularity is -1. The singularity is base-0, independent of base index of A.For example, if 2nd column of A is the same as first column, then A is singular and singularity = 1 which means `R(1,1)≈0`.

##### Returns

[Status](#T-CudaCSharp-Solver-Cuda-Status 'CudaCSharp.Solver.Cuda.Status')

##### Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| handle | [T:CudaCSharp.Solver.Cuda.Sparse.NativeMethods.SpQRSolveFunc\`1](#T-T-CudaCSharp-Solver-Cuda-Sparse-NativeMethods-SpQRSolveFunc`1 'T:CudaCSharp.Solver.Cuda.Sparse.NativeMethods.SpQRSolveFunc`1') | handle to the cuSolverSP library context. |

<a name='T-CudaCSharp-SparseMatrixFormat'></a>
## SparseMatrixFormat `type`

##### Namespace

CudaCSharp

##### Summary

The format specification enum of sparse matrix

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-SparseMatrixFormat-Any'></a>
### Any `constants`

##### Summary

Any of the atomic formats. Value = 111...111

##### Remarks

Since the atom formats are all orthogonal in binary, this kind of definition becomes useful.
If some custom formats are defined afterwards, this trick should still be used.

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-SparseMatrixFormat-COOC'></a>
### COOC `constants`

##### Summary

Coordinate Format (COO) that stores each non-zero element's `x` and `y` coordinates which are sorted in the column-first order. Value = 000...0010

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-SparseMatrixFormat-COOR'></a>
### COOR `constants`

##### Summary

Coordinate Format (COO) that stores each non-zero element's `x` and `y` coordinates which are sorted in the row-first order. Value = 000...0001

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-SparseMatrixFormat-CSC'></a>
### CSC `constants`

##### Summary

Compressed Sparse Column Format (CSC). The only way the CSC differs from the CSR format is that the column index array instead of row indices array stores the end-of-row offsets. Value = 000...01000

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-SparseMatrixFormat-CSR'></a>
### CSR `constants`

##### Summary

Compressed Sparse Row Format (CSR). The only way the CSR differs from the COO format is that the array containing the row indices is compressed in CSR format, that is, the row index array only stores the `LeadDim + 1` the end-of-row offsets of the value array. Value = 000...0100

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-SparseMatrixFormat-ColumnMajor'></a>
### ColumnMajor `constants`

##### Summary

The column majored formats. Value = 000...01010

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-SparseMatrixFormat-Compressed'></a>
### Compressed `constants`

##### Summary

Since [CSR](#F-CudaCSharp-SparseMatrixFormat-CSR 'CudaCSharp.SparseMatrixFormat.CSR') and [CSC](#F-CudaCSharp-SparseMatrixFormat-CSC 'CudaCSharp.SparseMatrixFormat.CSC') are so similar that it can be generalized to the Compressed Format. Value = 000...01100

##### Remarks

Since the atom formats are all orthogonal in binary, this kind of definition becomes useful.
If some custom formats are defined afterwards, this trick should still be used.

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-SparseMatrixFormat-Coordinated'></a>
### Coordinated `constants`

##### Summary

Since [COOC](#F-CudaCSharp-SparseMatrixFormat-COOC 'CudaCSharp.SparseMatrixFormat.COOC') and [COOR](#F-CudaCSharp-SparseMatrixFormat-COOR 'CudaCSharp.SparseMatrixFormat.COOR') are so similar that it can be generalized to the Coordinate Format (COO). Value = 000...0011

##### Remarks

Since the atom formats are all orthogonal in binary, this kind of definition becomes useful.
If some custom formats are defined afterwards, this trick should still be used.

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-SparseMatrixFormat-RowMajor'></a>
### RowMajor `constants`

##### Summary

The row majored formats. Value = 000...0101

<a name='T-CudaCSharp-Arrays-SparseVector`1'></a>
## SparseVector\`1 `type`

##### Namespace

CudaCSharp.Arrays

##### Summary

The sparse vector class that inherit the [VectorBase\`1](#T-CudaCSharp-Arrays-VectorBase`1 'CudaCSharp.Arrays.VectorBase`1') and implements the [IPrintable](#T-CudaCSharp-IPrintable 'CudaCSharp.IPrintable').

##### Generic Types

| Name | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| T | the supported data types are [Single](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Single 'System.Single'), [Double](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Double 'System.Double'), [FloatComplex](#T-CudaCSharp-FloatComplex 'CudaCSharp.FloatComplex'), [DoubleComplex](#T-CudaCSharp-DoubleComplex 'CudaCSharp.DoubleComplex'); other types of data causes [NotSupportedException](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.NotSupportedException 'System.NotSupportedException') |

##### Remarks

The indices array are platform specific, [Int64](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int64 'System.Int64') for 64-bit system and [Int32](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int32 'System.Int32') otherwise.

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-Status-AllocFailed'></a>
### AllocFailed `constants`

##### Summary

Resource allocation failed inside the cuBlas library. This is usually
caused by a cudaMalloc() failure.



To correct: prior to the function call, deallocate previously allocated
memory as much as possible.

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-Status-ArchMismatch'></a>
### ArchMismatch `constants`

##### Summary

The function requires a feature absent from the device architecture;
usually caused by the lack of support for atomic operations or double
precision.



To correct: compile and run the application on a device with compute
capability 2.0 or above.

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-Status-ExecutionFailed'></a>
### ExecutionFailed `constants`

##### Summary

The GPU program failed to execute. This is often caused by a launch
failure of the kernel on the GPU, which can be caused by multiple
reasons.



To correct: check that the hardware, an appropriate version of the
driver, and the cuSolver library are correctly installed.

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-Status-InternalError'></a>
### InternalError `constants`

##### Summary

An internal cuSolver operation failed. This error is usually caused by a
cudaMemcpyAsync() failure.



To correct: check that the hardware, an appropriate version of the
driver, and the cuSolver library are correctly installed. Also, check
that the memory passed as a parameter to the routine is not being
deallocated prior to the routine’s completion.

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-Status-InvalidValue'></a>
### InvalidValue `constants`

##### Summary

An unsupported value or parameter was passed to the function (a
negative vector size, for example).



To correct: ensure that all the parameters being passed have valid
values.

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-Status-LicenseError'></a>
### LicenseError `constants`

##### Summary



<a name='F-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-Status-MappingError'></a>
### MappingError `constants`

##### Summary



<a name='F-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-Status-NotInitialized'></a>
### NotInitialized `constants`

##### Summary

The cuBlas library was not initialized. This is usually caused by the
lack of a prior call, an error in the CUDA Runtime API called by the
cuSolver routine, or an error in the hardware setup.



To correct: call cuBlasCreate() prior to the function call; and
check that the hardware, an appropriate version of the driver, and the
cuSolver library are correctly installed.

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-Status-NotSupported'></a>
### NotSupported `constants`

##### Summary



<a name='F-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-Status-Success'></a>
### Success `constants`

##### Summary

The operation completed successfully

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-Rng-Cuda-Status-AllocationFailed'></a>
### AllocationFailed `constants`

##### Summary

Memory allocation failed.

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-Rng-Cuda-Status-ArchMismatch'></a>
### ArchMismatch `constants`

##### Summary

Architecture mismatch, GPU does not support requested feature.

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-Rng-Cuda-Status-DoublePrecisionRequired'></a>
### DoublePrecisionRequired `constants`

##### Summary

GPU does not have double precision required by MRG32k3a.

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-Rng-Cuda-Status-InitializationFailed'></a>
### InitializationFailed `constants`

##### Summary

Initialization of CUDA failed.

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-Rng-Cuda-Status-InternalError'></a>

### AllocFailed `constants`

##### Summary

Resource allocation failed inside the cuSolver library. This is usually
caused by a cudaMalloc() failure.



To correct: prior to the function call, deallocate previously allocated
memory as much as possible.

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-Solver-Cuda-Status-ArchMismatch'></a>
### ArchMismatch `constants`

##### Summary

The function requires a feature absent from the device architecture;
usually caused by the lack of support for atomic operations or double
precision.



To correct: compile and run the application on a device with compute
capability 2.0 or above.

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-Solver-Cuda-Status-ExecutionFailed'></a>
### ExecutionFailed `constants`

##### Summary

The GPU program failed to execute. This is often caused by a launch
failure of the kernel on the GPU, which can be caused by multiple
reasons.



To correct: check that the hardware, an appropriate version of the
driver, and the cuSolver library are correctly installed.

<a name='F-CudaCSharp-Solver-Cuda-Status-InternalError'></a>
### InternalError `constants`

##### Summary

An internal cuSolver operation failed. This error is usually caused by a
cudaMemcpyAsync() failure.



To correct: check that the hardware, an appropriate version of the
driver, and the cuSolver library are correctly installed. Also, check
that the memory passed as a parameter to the routine is not being
deallocated prior to the routine’s completion.

The function requires a feature absent from the device architecture; usually caused by the lack of support for atomic operations or double precision. To correct: compile and run the application on a device with appropriate compute capability, which is 1.1 for 32-bit atomic operations and 1.3 for double precision.

<a name='T-CudaCSharp-Memory-Storage`1'></a>
## Storage\`1 `type`

##### Namespace

CudaCSharp.Memory

##### Summary

The abstract wrapper class of raw device / host pointer [IntPtr](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.IntPtr 'System.IntPtr').

##### Generic Types

| Name | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| T | any sequential memory layout struct |

##### Remarks

I must warn you that although C# has GC to periodically collect unused garbage to prevent memory leak, you should not rely on it too much. to use `using` statement or call [Dispose](#M-CudaCSharp-Memory-Storage`1-Dispose 'CudaCSharp.Memory.Storage`1.Dispose') and/or [Dispose](#M-CudaCSharp-AbstractArray`1-Dispose 'CudaCSharp.AbstractArray`1.Dispose').
The leaked memory which will be collected GC still causes not only performance loss but also potential bugs if you do not know how GC works, since both [Storage\`1](#T-CudaCSharp-Memory-Storage`1 'CudaCSharp.Memory.Storage`1') and [AbstractArray\`1](#T-CudaCSharp-AbstractArray`1 'CudaCSharp.AbstractArray`1') are classes with finalizers thus cannot be in GC generation 0, i.e. they will not be immediately disposed when out-of-scope.
See https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/garbage-collection/ for official documentations of GC.

<a name='M-CudaCSharp-Arrays-TensorOrder-#ctor-System-Runtime-CompilerServices-ITuple-'></a>
### #ctor(tuple) `constructor`

##### Summary

Create an order from a general tuple whose element must be [Int16](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int16 'System.Int16'), [Int32](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int32 'System.Int32'), [Int64](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int64 'System.Int64'), [Index](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Index 'System.Index') or [Range](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Range 'System.Range') (base-zero order index and range, cannot be negative) or [Char](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Char 'System.Char') (character label which can only be checked when passed to a [DenseTensor\`1](#T-CudaCSharp-Arrays-DenseTensor`1 'CudaCSharp.Arrays.DenseTensor`1')).

##### Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| tuple | [System.Runtime.CompilerServices.ITuple](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Runtime.CompilerServices.ITuple 'System.Runtime.CompilerServices.ITuple') | the general tuple of any length to indicate the permutation order; specially, if an element is [All](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Range.All 'System.Range.All'), it is regarded as the rest of the indices in ascending order. |

##### Exceptions

| Name | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| [System.ArgumentNullException](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.ArgumentNullException 'System.ArgumentNullException') | if `tuple` is null or of zero length |
| [System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException 'System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException') | if any of the `tuple` elements is not of the allowed types |
| [System.ArgumentException](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.ArgumentException 'System.ArgumentException') | if there are duplicated indices or more than one [All](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Range.All 'System.Range.All') in `tuple` |

an array of [Int32](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.Int32 'System.Int32') of base-zero indicating the permutation order

##### Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| tensor | [CudaCSharp.ITensor](#T-CudaCSharp-ITensor 'CudaCSharp.ITensor') | the target tensor |

##### Exceptions

| Name | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| [System.ArgumentNullException](http://msdn.microsoft.com/query/dev14.query?appId=Dev14IDEF1&l=EN-US&k=k:System.ArgumentNullException 'System.ArgumentNullException') | if `tensor` or its [Label](#P-CudaCSharp-ITensor-Label 'CudaCSharp.ITensor.Label') is null |

<a name='M-CudaCSharp-Arrays-VectorBase`1-AddBy_αx_Opposite-CudaCSharp-Arrays-VectorBase{`0},`0-'></a>
### AddBy_αx_Opposite(y,α) `method`

##### Summary

Compute $\vec{y} = \vec{y} + \alpha \vec{v}_{\text{this}}$, always in-place for non-sparse `y`.

##### Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| y | [CudaCSharp.Arrays.VectorBase{\`0}](#T-CudaCSharp-Arrays-VectorBase{`0} 'CudaCSharp.Arrays.VectorBase{`0}') | [VectorBase\`1](#T-CudaCSharp-Arrays-VectorBase`1 'CudaCSharp.Arrays.VectorBase`1') to be altered by this method |
| α | [\`0](#T-`0 '`0') | scalar of type `T` |

##### Remarks

The opposite of [AddBy_αx](#M-CudaCSharp-Arrays-VectorBase`1-AddBy_αx-CudaCSharp-Arrays-VectorBase{`0},`0- 'CudaCSharp.Arrays.VectorBase`1.AddBy_αx(CudaCSharp.Arrays.VectorBase{`0},`0)'), only the classes directly inherits [VectorBase\`1](#T-CudaCSharp-Arrays-VectorBase`1 'CudaCSharp.Arrays.VectorBase`1') need to implement this method. This method is used by built-in [DenseVector\`1](#T-CudaCSharp-Arrays-DenseVector`1 'CudaCSharp.Arrays.DenseVector`1') and [SparseVector\`1](#T-CudaCSharp-Arrays-SparseVector`1 'CudaCSharp.Arrays.SparseVector`1') to implement [AddBy_αx](#M-CudaCSharp-Arrays-VectorBase`1-AddBy_αx-CudaCSharp-Arrays-VectorBase{`0},`0- 'CudaCSharp.Arrays.VectorBase`1.AddBy_αx(CudaCSharp.Arrays.VectorBase{`0},`0)').

<a name='T-CudaCSharp-Solver-Mkl-NativeMethods-compSchurFunc`1'></a>
## compSchurFunc\`1 `type`

##### Namespace

CudaCSharp.Solver.Mkl.NativeMethods

##### Summary

Computes the eigenvalues and real Schur factorization of a general matrix, and orders the factorization so that selected eigenvalues are at the top left of the Schur form.

##### Returns

The info. If `info == 0`, the operation is successful; if `info == -i`, the `i`parameter is wrong (not counting handle).
If `info ≤ `, the QR algorithm failed to compute all the eigenvalues; `w` contain those eigenvalues which have converged; if `jobv` is 'V', `V` contains the matrix which reduces `A` to its partially converged Schur form.
If `info ≤ +1`, the eigenvalues could not be reordered because some eigenvalues were too close to separate (the problem is very ill-conditioned).
If `info ≤ +2`, after reordering, round-off changed values of some complex eigenvalues so that leading eigenvalues in the Schur form no longer satisfy ` ≠ 0`; this could also be caused by underflow due to scaling.

##### Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| matrix_layout | [T:CudaCSharp.Solver.Mkl.NativeMethods.compSchurFunc\`1](#T-T-CudaCSharp-Solver-Mkl-NativeMethods-compSchurFunc`1 'T:CudaCSharp.Solver.Mkl.NativeMethods.compSchurFunc`1') | [MklSolverLayout](#T-CudaCSharp-Solver-Mkl-MklSolverLayout 'CudaCSharp.Solver.Mkl.MklSolverLayout') of matrix `A` |

<a name='T-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-NativeMethods-geamFunc`1'></a>
## geamFunc\`1 `type`

##### Namespace

CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.NativeMethods

##### Summary

This function performs the matrix-matrix addition/transposition `C` = `α``opA`(`A`) + `β``opB`(`B`)
where `α` and `β` are scalars; `A`, `B`, `C` are matrices stored in column-major format with dimensions `opA`(`A`) -- `m`×`n`, `opB`(`B`) -- `m`×`n` and `C` -- `m`×`n`, respectively. 
Also, for matrix `A`,
`opA`(`A`) = `A` if `opA` == [None](#F-CudaCSharp-MatrixOperation-None 'CudaCSharp.MatrixOperation.None');
`opA`(`A`) = `A`^T if `opA` == [Transpose](#F-CudaCSharp-MatrixOperation-Transpose 'CudaCSharp.MatrixOperation.Transpose');
`opA`(`A`) = `A`^H if `opA` == [ConjugateTranspose](#F-CudaCSharp-MatrixOperation-ConjugateTranspose 'CudaCSharp.MatrixOperation.ConjugateTranspose').
The same for `B`.

##### Returns

operation status enum [Status](#T-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-Status 'CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.Status')

##### Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| handle | [T:CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.NativeMethods.geamFunc\`1](#T-T-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-NativeMethods-geamFunc`1 'T:CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.NativeMethods.geamFunc`1') | handle to the CUDA BLAS library context |

##### Remarks

The operation is out-of-place if `C` does not overlap `A` or `B`.



The in-place mode supports the following two operations, `C` = `α``C` + `β``opB`(`B`) and `C` = `α``opA`(`A`) + `β` C.
If ` == `, `ldc` = `lda` and `opA` = [None](#F-CudaCSharp-MatrixOperation-None 'CudaCSharp.MatrixOperation.None'), or If ` ==  &&  ==  &&  == `, in-place mode will be used.
If the user does not meet above requirements, [InvalidValue](#F-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-Status-InvalidValue 'CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.Status.InvalidValue') is returned.

<a name='T-CudaCSharp-Solver-Mkl-NativeMethods-realSchurFunc`1'></a>
## realSchurFunc\`1 `type`

##### Namespace

CudaCSharp.Solver.Mkl.NativeMethods

##### Summary

Computes the eigenvalues and real Schur factorization of a general matrix, and orders the factorization so that selected eigenvalues are at the top left of the Schur form.

##### Returns

The info. If `info == 0`, the operation is successful; if `info == -i`, the `i`parameter is wrong (not counting handle).
If `info ≤ `, the QR algorithm failed to compute all the eigenvalues; `wr` and `wi` contain those eigenvalues which have converged; if `jobv` is 'V', `V` contains the matrix which reduces `A` to its partially converged Schur form.
If `info ≤ +1`, the eigenvalues could not be reordered because some eigenvalues were too close to separate (the problem is very ill-conditioned).
If `info ≤ +2`, after reordering, round-off changed values of some complex eigenvalues so that leading eigenvalues in the Schur form no longer satisfy ` ≠ 0`; this could also be caused by underflow due to scaling.

##### Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| matrix_layout | [T:CudaCSharp.Solver.Mkl.NativeMethods.realSchurFunc\`1](#T-T-CudaCSharp-Solver-Mkl-NativeMethods-realSchurFunc`1 'T:CudaCSharp.Solver.Mkl.NativeMethods.realSchurFunc`1') | [MklSolverLayout](#T-CudaCSharp-Solver-Mkl-MklSolverLayout 'CudaCSharp.Solver.Mkl.MklSolverLayout') of matrix `A` |

<a name='T-CudaCSharp-Solver-Mkl-NativeMethods-syevdFunc'></a>
## syevdFunc `type`

##### Namespace

CudaCSharp.Solver.Mkl.NativeMethods

##### Summary

This function computes the all eigenvalues and, optionally, all eigenvectors of a matrix.

##### Returns

The info. If `info = 0`, the process is successful. if `info = -i`, the i-th parameter is wrong. If `info = i`, and `jobz = 'N'`, then the algorithm failed to converge; i indicates the number of off-diagonal elements of an intermediate tridiagonal form which did not converge to zero. If `info = i`, and `jobz = 'V'`, then the algorithm failed to compute an eigenvalue while working on the sub-matrix lying in rows and columns `info/(n+1)` through `mod(info, n+1)`.

##### Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| matrix_layout | [T:CudaCSharp.Solver.Mkl.NativeMethods.syevdFunc](#T-T-CudaCSharp-Solver-Mkl-NativeMethods-syevdFunc 'T:CudaCSharp.Solver.Mkl.NativeMethods.syevdFunc') | [MklSolverLayout](#T-CudaCSharp-Solver-Mkl-MklSolverLayout 'CudaCSharp.Solver.Mkl.MklSolverLayout') of matrix `A` |

<a name='T-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-NativeMethods-syrkFunc`1'></a>
## syrkFunc\`1 `type`

##### Namespace

CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.NativeMethods

##### Summary

This function performs the symmetric/Hermitian rank-k update  `C` = `α``op`(`A`) `op`(`A`)^T + `β``C` ; where `α` and `β` are scalars, `C` is a symmetric matrix stored in lower or upper mode, and `A` is a matrix with dimensions `op`(`A`) `n`×`k`.

##### Returns

operation status enum [Status](#T-CudaCSharp-Blas-Cuda-Status 'CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.Status')

##### Parameters
